sources.title: Barbados Parliament: Cultural Industries Development Act, 2013 (amended copy)
sources.said: “approved producer of audio-visual content” or “approved producer ” means a film production company incorporated under the Companies Act, … (c) media - broadcast media including television, radio and cable, digital media including software and computer services, film and video, … (3) Where an approved producer referred to in subsection (1) has in an income year incurred expenditure for the purpose of the production and acquisition in respect of local films, then in calculating the assessable income of the approved producer for an income year, there shall be a write-off of 100 per cent.

items.notes: Part VII speaks of 'audio-visual content' and 'local films'; television is a cultural industry under s.2, but the Act names no series terms. A tax deduction, not a credit: what it is worth depends on the producer's income and rate, which the game would need from Barbados's income tax.

sources.title: National Cultural Foundation: Cultural Industries Development Fund
sources.said: The Cultural Industries Development Fund is open to all citizens of Barbados and companies registered in Barbados whose principal shareholder or partner is a citizen of the island. … Creative entrepreneurs are limited to one grant disbursement within a 12-month period and one disbursement per cultural project. … Project Execution funding is provided to creative entrepreneurs seeking assistance to complete a cultural or creative project that provides opportunities to market, promote and showcase the cultural product or service or to generate revenue through the sale of artistic or creative work. (Up to $30,000)

value.eligible: Barbadian citizens, and companies whose principal shareholder or partner is a citizen; registered on barbadosartists.bb

items.notes: Any cultural project, so a series or a play; no rate of yes published.

sources.said: § 1. 1) Fyri filmar, sendirøðir og heimildarfilmar, sum verða framleidd í Føroyum, verða 25% av útreiðslunum, sum eru hildnar í Føroyum, afturbornar, um umsøkjarin lýkur treytirnar fyri at fáa afturbering. Afturberingin er í mesta lagi 5 milliónir kr., sbr. tó stk. 2. … Stk. 2. 1) Lýsingar, tíðindi, veruleikasendingar, undirhaldssendingar og ítóttasendingar hava ikki rætt til afturbering eftir hesi løgtingslóg. … Stk. 2. Kravt verður, at høvuðsframleiðarin hevur framleitt í minsta lagi ein film ella eina sendirøð seinastu fimm árini undan umsóknini. … § 4. Afturbering av útreiðslum verður bert veitt føroyskum partafelag ella smápartafelag. … b) Fíggjarætlanin fyri framleiðsluna skal vísa, at í minsta lagi 500.000 kr. eru brúktar til útreiðslur, sum eru fevndar av § 8. … 3) Í minsta lagi 25% av fíggjarætlanini fyri framleiðsluna í Føroyum skal vera útlendsk fígging. … 4) Skjalprógvast skal, at avtala er um altjóða útbreiðslu av framleiðsluni.

sources.title: NZFC: New Zealand Screen Production Rebate, Criteria for New Zealand Productions, 1 July 2026 v.1.0
sources.said: The New Zealand Rebate is 40% of QNZPE. The New Zealand Rebate is capped at $12 million per production. … a series or season of a series whether scripted or unscripted including but not limited to drama, documentary, factual, reality, children’s and animation being a programme with a common theme or themes consisting of at least two episodes that are intended for release together in a national market or markets. Each episode (with the exception of animation) must be a least one commercial half-hour in length; or … Series of programmes – scripted … $1 million total and no less than $500,000 per hour … $10 million total per season … The proportion of non-New Zealand Government Production Funding for a television or other non-feature film production must be 25% of the Production Budget or higher. … A television or other non-feature film production must achieve 20 points or more (including the minimum points required in sections A and C) in the Significant New Zealand Content Test.

sources.title: NZFC: Rebate for New Zealand Productions
sources.said: Series - Scripted … NZ$1 million total … and at least NZ$500,000 per hour … or NZ$10 million per season … Other formats: At least 25% non-NZ government funding and 10% market attachments.

value.distribution: a secure confirmed commercial agreement for NZ distribution on an appropriate platform

items.notes: A New Zealand series (passing the Significant New Zealand Content Test) gets the same 40% as a feature, but its threshold is per hour of the production (total QNZPE over its duration in hours), or NZ$10m for a season. Every half-hour and hour episode the game makes clears the half-hour minimum. International productions get 20% (+5% points test) under separate criteria not re-read here.

sources.title: WIPO Lex: Закон Республики Таджикистан «О кино» (9 декабря 2004, № 67)
sources.said: фильм – аудиовизуальное произведение , созданное в художественной , хроникально документальной , научно - популярной , учебной , анимационной , телевизионной или иной форме … Государственное финансирование производства национального фильма , как правило , не может превышать 70 процентов сметной стоимости его производства . … В исключительных случаях с учетом художественной и культурной значимости кинопроекта и необходимости показа фильма на телеэкране , уполномоченный орган принимает решение о государственном финансировании фильма в размере до 100 процентов сметной стоимости его производства .
sources.quotes: Law of the Republic of Tajikistan On Cinema, No. 67 of 9 December 2004

value.exceptionWhen: artistic and cultural significance and the need to show the film on television

items.notes: A 'film' includes a television form, so a national series can be state-funded on the law's terms; the authorised body's yearly budget and selection rate aren't known.

sources.title: Tourism Committee of Uzbekistan (gov.uz): New milestone in tourism promotion: Uzbekistan launches rebate program to attract international film productions (2026-07-10)
sources.said: The Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan has adopted Resolution No. 372 of July 8, 2026, “On Supporting the Broad Implementation of a System to Enhance the Tourism Attractiveness of the Republic of Uzbekistan Through Film.” … 10% for expenditures of up to UZS 3 billion; … 15% for expenditures ranging from UZS 3 billion to UZS 5 billion; … 20% for expenditures ranging from UZS 5 billion to UZS 10 billion; … 25% for expenditures exceeding UZS 10 billion. … The maximum reimbursement available for a single film project will be UZS 4 billion. … UZS 5 billion has been allocated from the 2026 State Budget to finance reimbursements for foreign film productions.

value.for: foreign film companies shooting in Uzbekistan

items.notes: The notice speaks of 'films' and 'film projects'; whether a series qualifies needs the resolution's text (lex.uz searches for it returned nothing). Whether the rates step by bracket or apply to the whole spend isn't said. Foreign companies only.
